row.evidence: WordPress.com's plans (Personal to Commerce, plus Enterprise via WordPress VIP) list no SCIM or SAML features; sign-in is WordPress.com's own 'Secure Sign-On', users are invited per site, and searches of the support centre, REST API reference and VIP docs found no SCIM.
row.notes: Researched as WordPress.com (Automattic), the hosted WordPress product, with WordPress VIP as its Enterprise tier; self-hosted WordPress is open-source software, not a SaaS subscription. Plans are priced per site with unlimited users (Personal $4, Premium $8, Business $25, Commerce $45 per month billed yearly), so per-user prices are null. No SCIM endpoint is documented anywhere. WordPress.com 'Secure Sign-On' means WordPress.com accounts, not SAML. WordPress VIP supports SAML SSO for the VIP Dashboard and, through a SAML plugin, for WordPress logins. Users are managed by invitation, in the dashboard or through the REST API (list, invite, update, delete per site). Okta's 'WordPress.com' OIN app is SWA only. Okta's separate 'Wordpress' app advertises SCIM/REST provisioning for self-hosted WordPress sites, which is not a WordPress.com feature.

scim.notes: available=false is by absence: no SCIM in the pricing page, WordPress.com support search, REST API reference or WordPress VIP docs search/sitemap.

capabilities.notes: Users join a site by invitation to an existing WordPress.com account; there is no create-user endpoint in the reference. Removal is per site.

endpoints.purpose: List the users of a site
Get a site user by login
Update a site user's details (including role)
Invite one or more users to a site
Delete or remove a user from a site

okta.notes: OIN page markup marks only SWA as checked for the WordPress.com app. Okta also lists a separate 'Wordpress' app (https://www.okta.com/integrations/wordpress/) with SAML, SCIM and Create/Update/Deactivate for self-hosted WordPress; it is not a WordPress.com integration.

fallbacks.notes: WordPress.com accounts sign in with WordPress.com Secure Sign-On; WordPress VIP sites can add a SAML plugin, whose JIT behaviour depends on the plugin.
